children: (Nasdaq: TREO) (“Tactical” or the “Company”), a U.S.-focused rare earth elements company, today provided an update on its initial plans to advance its Peak Project in Hudspeth County, Texas following its Nasdaq listing.
Peak Project Core Fundamentals
Independent testing.
Work to date has been supported by APEX Geoscience, Kemetco Research, Forte Dynamics and the University of Texas at Austin.
Heavy rare earth profile.
Analytical work showed heavy rare earth elements plus yttrium averaging 2.09 times the light rare earth elements.
Material already mined.

Two decades of railway ballast crushing at the Sierra Blanca Quarry produced pre-crushed fines materials that are stockpiled on surface. The Company’s 2022 technical report described the material as already mined, crushed, conveyed and stockpiled.
Secured feedstock position.
The pre-crushed fines stockpiled material is accessible to Tactical under a 2026 purchase and sale agreement, together with an option over the quarry operation itself.

Ranjeet Sundher, Chief Executive Officer of Tactical, said, “Peak is a very special project in this sector because the potential feedstock material is already out of the ground. Two decades of quarry operations produced it, and it is sitting on surface in West Texas. Our technical work has concentrated on whether that material can be processed, and on the heavy rare earth profile it carries, which is where the United States is most exposed. With the Nasdaq listing complete, we are moving the project into its next phase.”
Peak’s Rare Earth Momentum
Work Completed to Date

Since acquiring its interest in the Peak Project, Tactical has advanced work across field sampling, independent assaying, quality assurance and quality control, mineralogical studies, drone surveys, scoping metallurgical testing, sample characterization, bench-scale leach testing, vat-leach testing, permeability testing and project planning. This work has established a technical base for the next work program, which includes exploration and an assessment of mineral resources.
Independent Geological Foundation

Tactical’s 2021 program collected samples from the active and historical quarry areas. The samples were analyzed by an independent accredited laboratory, reviewed by independent Qualified Persons, who found that the data were suitable for the report and potential future mineral resource modelling.

In September 2022, Tactical filed the initial NI 43-101 / SK-1300 technical report for Peak. Prepared by APEX Geoscience Ltd. and Kemetco Research Inc., the report summarized the Company’s 2021 and 2022 exploration and metallurgical work and set out recommendations for a two-phase work program.
Heavy Rare Earth Element and Mineralogical Profile

Tactical’s analytical dataset (n=40 samples) showed that heavy rare earth elements plus yttrium (“HREE+Y”) averaged 2.9 times the light rare earth elements (“LREE”). Additionally, independent samples collected by the Qualified Person during a site inspection (n=8 samples) returned a comparable profile and validated the HREE mineralization and other elements. The material also showed enrichment in lithium, niobium, rubidium, yttrium and zirconium.

Mineralogical work at the University of Texas at Austin identified accessory minerals including cassiterite, columbite, yttrofluorite, yttrocerite, thorite and zircon. Two drone surveys completed by Texas registered land surveyors mapped the active pre-crushed fines stockpile.
Metallurgical Results

Initial metallurgical test work conducted by Kemetco assessed direct-leach amenability and maximum extraction potential across four leach conditions. Results from all four are reported below. Extraction response varied widely by reagent and test condition, from less than 25.3 percent to 96.1 percent.
Preliminary total rare earth elements plus yttrium (“TREE+Y”) extraction rates were as follows:
Ambient-temperature hydrochloric acid bottle-roll: less than 25.3 percent
Ambient-temperature sulfuric acid bottle-roll: 88 percent to 93 percent
Heated sulfuric acid agitated-tank: 89 percent to 90 percent
Heated hydrochloric acid agitated-tank: 95.6 percent to 96.1 percent

The work also identified lithium as a potential by-product for further study. Heated hydrochloric acid agitated-tank tests returned lithium extraction results of 66.2 percent to 87.6 percent, while acid-bake and water-leach tests returned 90 percent to 96 percent lithium extraction.

These were scoping-scale results from composite samples. They do not establish commercial-scale recovery. Further work is required on material variability, reagent consumption, impurity removal, leach-solution processing, production of saleable products, water balance, and by-product and waste handling.
Phase 1 Metallurgical Work Program

In May 2024, Tactical reported that sample characterization, bench-scale leach testing, vat-leach testing and permeability testing had been completed, with data analysis and reporting in progress. Currently, column-leach testing results and internal desktop benchmarking and scoping studies are ongoing.

The programs were designed to build an initial geometallurgical database, assess leaching at fine and coarse particle sizes, evaluate hydraulic conductivity of potential feed blends and identify project value drivers. Tactical also engaged Forte Dynamics Inc. to review available data, conduct a gap analysis and develop a roadmap toward a preliminary economic assessment.

The 2022 technical report recommended future sonic drilling, geophysical surveys, core sampling and bench- and column-scale metallurgical testing, followed, if warranted, by advanced metallurgy, demonstration plant planning, permitting and environmental work, community engagement and technical reporting.
Next Phase of Technical Work

Building on the work completed to date and pending the receipt and review of the results from the Phase-1 Metallurgical Work Program, Tactical is starting to pre-plan the next phase of work at the Peak Project. Key areas of focus are intended to include
Finalizing Phase-1 work program results
Advancing process development
Developing permitting and environmental roadmaps
Growing downstream strategic partnerships
Establishing engineering workflows
Expanding exploration and geological studies
Updating Technical Reports
The company’s immediate efforts are aimed at accelerating project growth and development activities in support of future fast-tracked production decisions.
Project Background

Peak is located within the active Sierra Blanca Quarry, approximately 90 miles southeast of El Paso. The project focuses on rare earth-enriched pre-crushed fines stockpiles generated by quarry operations. The Company’s 2022 NI 43-101 / SK-1300 technical report described the material as already mined, crushed, conveyed and stockpiled, and identified road access, a rail spur, power and space for project work at the quarry.
Secured Feedstock Position

In March 2026, Tactical entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement with Sierra Blanca Quarry, LLC covering approximately four million tons of pre-crushed fines stockpiled material generated by the ballast crushing plant, rights to additional stockpiled fines materials produced thereafter, and an exclusive option to acquire 100 percent of the membership interests of Sierra Blanca Quarry, LLC through a blend of cash and stock. The agreement has an initial term expiring July 31, 2036. In April 2026, the Company entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement converting approximately 1.5 million tons of that fines materials access into secured ownership, the first tranche within a staged acquisition strategy. The agreements remain subject to their respective terms and conditions.

No mineral resources or mineral reserves have been estimated for the pre-crushed fines stockpiled material. The tonnage figures above are derived from the Company’s commercial agreements rather than from an estimate of mineral resources or mineral reserves.

The Company’s common shares began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “TREO” on August 20, 2026. The listing provides access to U.S. capital markets as Tactical continues technical, engineering and permitting work at Peak.
Technical Disclosure

The scientific and technical information in this release is based on the Company’s NI 43-101 technical / SK-1300 report with an effective date of September 15, 2022, and prior Company disclosures. The Peak Project remains an early-stage project, and Tactical has not completed mineral resource estimation work.

Roy Eccles P. Geol. of APEX Geoscience Ltd., an independent “qualified person” as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects and is independent of the company, has reviewed and approved the geologic scientific and technical information in this press release as they relate to the geological sections of the technical report he is responsible for.

Norman Chow M.A.Sc., P. Eng. President of Kemetco Research Inc., an independent “qualified person” as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects and is independent of the Company, has reviewed and approved the metallurgical scientific and technical information in this press release as they relate to the sections of technical report he is responsible for.
About Tactical Resources

Tactical Resources is a natural resources company focused on rare earth elements critical to advanced technologies, including semiconductors, electric vehicles, robotics, aerospace systems, and national defense applications. The Company is advancing the Peak Project in Hudspeth County, Texas, as part of its strategy to help build a secure domestic supply chain, reduce reliance on foreign-controlled sources and strengthen North American critical mineral security.

Tactical Resources is also pursuing innovative metallurgical processing and separation technologies designed to improve the economics, scalability, and sustainability of rare earth production. Through this integrated approach, the Company aims to become a key participant in the rapidly growing U.S. critical minerals ecosystem.
